plan.h: Round 3: cut r3 is an attempt at everything you've noted so far (Kai: "however wrong that might be"). Note it again.
items: Office to the seasons (0:00 to 3:26) is re-cut from the clips. From 'Viral' on (3:26 to the end) is still Jack's Karen v4, untouched.
Your earlier notes are pinned to the OLD cut's times, so their pins now sit on different shots. They're answered below as before.
Grey 'NEW SHOT TO MAKE' cards = shots that don't exist yet (the coffee shop, Karen shouting at her phone). Nothing has been spent in Flow.
0:08 coffee-shop card in place of the phone shot.
0:34 Karen stunned → hands the laptop back → Sean's screen: 'Your role has also been made redundant' → the boss reacts → defenestrate.
0:54 Night out (the bar tab was never in this take) → river: Karen shouts at Sean (her voice, Gacrux) → the throw (flicker trimmed) → phone sinking → Susan: 'Karen, you mad lad' (Kore).
1:27 Morning: 'Lesson learned...' over the river, punchline on Karen waking, Susan-asleep shot gone.
1:40 Phone box: Susan's reminder (narrator) → grey flashback to the river with Karen's vow → 'Karen, well... she rolls her sleeves up' (the bed speech cut off the front of the same take).

2:10 Calling everyone: 'New York is about to experience...' → pin → MARTHA, receptionist → pin → CLIVE, local council → pin → HARRIET, borough representative. Each gets one of Jack's existing berating lines.
2:59 All day: 'Karen's conquest will take patience.' → 'I have ALL DAY to complain' → All night (night) / All month (rain) / All year (snow) → Guinness → 'A new day, a new dawn...' → Viral.

It's LONGER, not snappier: the new section runs 3:26 where v4's ran 2:57, because I kept every existing joke line and added the new beats. Cutting jokes is your call, not mine. The obvious ones to lose: 'A new day, a new dawn... sniper' (the seasons now say it), and one of the two long berating lines (souls / savours each syllable).
Karen's shout sits on a still card for 11 s; it will play better once that shot exists.

New lines are drafts by me unless the words were yours: the laptop line, Susan's reminder, the three name intros, 'All night / month / year'. Yours: the shout, 'mad lad', 'New York is about to experience...', 'conquest will take patience'.
Note this cut on the page, same as before: anything, anywhere.
Which lines to drop for speed (above), or I keep everything until you've watched it.
When you're happy with the shape, I make the two missing shots in Flow (stills first, for you to approve).

replies.at229: In cut r3 as a grey 'NEW SHOT TO MAKE' card: Karen in a coffee shop, finger pointed at the barista. The real shot waits for the Flow round (still first, you approve).
replies.at1075: In cut r3: Karen stunned (43) → 'Stunned, Karen hands the laptop back to her boss' over her handing it over (end of new clip 5) → Sean's screen, 'Your role has also been made redundant' (made from the existing screen) with 'Ay-Eye Sean fires him too'.
replies.at1135: In cut r3: the boss's reaction is the shocked part of new clip 42, then the defenestrate line over Karen's eyes. No new footage needed; if it's not enough, a new reaction shot goes in the Flow round.
replies.at1511: In cut r3: flicker trimmed (the throw now starts 4 frames later). Karen's shout (Gacrux) plays on a placeholder card for the new shot, then the throw, the phone sinking, and Susan's 'Karen, you mad lad' (Kore).
replies.at1599: Agreed in round 1: the Susan-asleep shot goes, Karen waking moves up, and 'In these moments, even atheists pray to Christ' lands on her. Edit only.
replies.at1649: Yes, it's recorded (round 1, the note at 1:06): this scene is dropped.
replies.at2213: In cut r3: 'Susan reminds her. Last night, Karen threw her phone in the river... and swore to make the biggest complaint the world has ever seen.'
replies.at2230: In cut r3: no bar tab anywhere (the 0:50 line in the cut never had it), and 'Susan explains that A.I. Sean fired her' is gone.
replies.at2343: In cut r3: the narrator tells it (Susan's reminder line), then the flashback carries Karen's vow.
replies.at2383: In cut r3: the night-time box is gone; the canonical daytime box runs throughout. Night only comes back in the seasons montage ('All night').
replies.at2502: In cut r3: the 'People like Susan lie in bed...' speech is cut; only 'Karen, well... she rolls her sleeves up...' stays.
replies.at2624: Done in cut r3: Susan's reminder → a grey flashback to the river with Karen's own 'complaint of the century' (echoed) → 'Karen, well... she rolls her sleeves up and actually does something about it' on the canonical daytime box (new clip 46; I wrongly called the box 'new clip 12' before, that's the aerial). Flashback re-uses the river shots, no new clip.
replies.at2872: Cut r3 tries it: your line opens the stretch ('New York is about to experience a level of complaining it never thought possible. Every borough had better prepare.') over the aerial, then pins drop on the map, zooming pin to pin. The old 13-second 'Enraged by the injustice... receptionist level' intro is gone.
replies.at3072: Cut r3 tries the whole shape: pin → 'First: Martha. She's just a receptionist.' (with a name caption) → one berating line → zoom out, next pin → Clive, local council → Harriet, borough representative → 'Poor bastards.' Then 'Karen's conquest will take patience' → 'I have ALL DAY to complain' → All night (night box) / All month (rain) / All year (snow), fast. The berating lines are Jack's existing ones, reshuffled; the name intros are mine. It came out longer than v4, see 'What I know is off'.

I think that as these first few shots are really setting up the archetype in people's heads, we should really lean into that as opposed to this scene where she's just looking down at the phone.

And then I want another scene of AI Sean firing him as well. Because that's the drama. Like, don't forget the end of this story is where AI Sean fires the president live on TV. So, like, this is an escalation thing we're setting up here. So I think it's very much like we need to include that part in the scene here.

And it sets up like she's old school, you know, which is why she's in the payphone and it sets the whole thing up.

at2872.note: So, I think this whole scene from now onwards is about escalation, and so I think this shot especially is like the city of New York is about to experience a level of complaining it never thought possible. Every borough had better prepare for the onslaught. So, we set up the stage, and then we've got the map, and what I really want is this sequence of Karen being like ringing up, complaining, hours later ringing the next person, and we're like leaping all over the city. Now, it kind of feels like that's what we've got here, but it needs to be a bit more snappier and a bit more energetic. So, it's like Karen has called everybody is really the thing. So, I want us please to really have a look into like how we might be able to do that using the current approach.

at3072.note: So, for example, like, at the moment, we're kind of narrating this beginning, the beginning of, like, Karen is going to call everybody. It's already taken 20 seconds. I think we are indulging ourselves far too much in the audience's attention. I think what we can do is be, like, if we set it up right, Karen is about to unleash the complaining of a champion. First, it's Martha. She's just a receptionist. We could almost name each person, and Karen's interaction with the person could be narrated, and then we zoom out on the map and zoom into a pin on the map, and it's like at least three of those in quick succession gives you the idea that Karen is, like, a masterful phone operator. Meanwhile, she's in the phone box. Then I think we cut to, like, how long she's in the phone box, and so thinking about it, I think we do these two parts one after the other. The first is, like, you know, she's leaping all over the map, speaking to everybody. The second is she is now spending a long time in this phone box, and we need to get an intense version of both of those things across fairly quickly, so in terms of she's speaking to loads of people all over the map, I think it's the, you know, we introduce the character. We look at a pin on the map. We introduce the character. We explain how Karen berated them, and we escalate, and what does escalate look like? We're looking back at the map. We zoom out of that pin and zoom into another pin, and now it's the next character, and if we do that three times, then Karen has spoken to three managers in very quick succession. Then the narrator needs to be, like, you know, ultimately, Karen's conquest will take patience, but she's got all day to complain, and I think the narrator saying that now, then we cut into the seasons transitioning, and so I think we can do, like, you know, it's summer today, but she's there all night. The next day, it's raining. She's there all month. The next month is full. She's here all year. Now it's snowing, something like that, like an equivalent fast-cut progression through the seasons, so now we've done she's calling everybody, and she's waited ages, and both of those have happened in quite quick succession, so that kind of fundamentally changes a whole chunk of the next scene, but I just want you to absorb this, and then we'll make a plan for what we do.
